papers.title: Strong Lower Bounds for Weak Epsilon-Nets
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a finite point set in $\mathbb{R}^d$. A \emph{weak $\varepsilon$-net} for $P$ with respect to convex sets is a finite set $X\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ intersecting every convex set containing at least $\varepsilon|P|$ points of $P$. Determining their optimal worst-case size was described by Alon, Kalai, Matousek, and Meshulam [Adv. Appl. Math., 2002] as \emph{``one of the truly important open problems in combinatorial geometry.''} We give elementary constructions which establish the first polynomially superlinear lower bounds in fixed dimension. Already in $\mathbb{R}^3$, we construct point sets for which every weak $\varepsilon$-net has size $\Omega(\varepsilon^{-3/2})$. More generally, for every fixed $d\ge3$, we obtain a lower bound of $\Omega_d(\varepsilon^{-\gamma_d})$, where $\gamma_d=\sqrt{d/2}+O(1)$. Consequently, no upper bound of the form $O_d(\varepsilon^{-C})$ can hold with an absolute constant $C$ which is independent of the dimension. Despite the recent progress on upper bounds, the strongest previous general lower bound remained $\Omega_d(\varepsilon^{-1}\log^{d-1}(1/\varepsilon))$, due to Bukh, Matousek, and Nivasch [Israel J. Math., 2011]. To obtain our results, we apply a quadratic lift to grid-based configurations with many point-line incidences. The bounds also yield polynomial separations between fractional and integral piercing numbers of convex families, and lower bounds for Hadwiger--Debrunner numbers.

papers.title: Implicit Additively Weighted Geodesic Voronoi Diagrams and Applications
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a simple polygon with $m$ vertices. After $O(m)$-time preprocessing of $P$, for any set $S$ of $n$ additively weighted point sites, we compute an implicit additively weighted geodesic Voronoi diagram in $O(n\log n+n\log^2 m)$ time, supporting nearest-neighbor queries in $O(\log(n+m))$ time. In contrast, explicitly constructing the diagram requires $\Omega(m)$ time. Our algorithm introduces a new sweep-line paradigm that avoids explicitly constructing the diagram, together with a novel technique for point location in implicit subdivisions. As applications, we obtain new dynamic data structures for additively weighted geodesic nearest-neighbor searching and the first efficient algorithms for shortest paths in geodesic disk graphs. After the same $O(m)$-time preprocessing, single-source shortest paths in a geodesic disk graph of $n$ sites can be computed in $O(n\log n+n\log^2 m)$ time in the unweighted case and $O(n^{3/2}(\log n+\log^2 m))$ time in the weighted case. We also extend our techniques to implicit farthest geodesic Voronoi diagrams for unweighted sites, obtaining analogous bounds and dynamic farthest-neighbor data structures.

papers.title: Optimal Average Distortion for Non-Expansive Embeddings of Euclidean Metrics into the Line: With applications to cut-matching games and vertex expansion
papers.abstract: We show that any $n$-point Euclidean metric admits a non-expansive embedding into the line with average distortion at most $O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}}\right)$, matching a known lower bound. We also present two applications of this result. First, we give a cut-player strategy with an optimal spectral guarantee for the undirected cut-matching game. Second, we give an improved spectral approximation for vertex expansion in high-degree graphs.

papers.title: A General Theoretical Framework for Transformed Geometric Pattern Matching in Music
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a framework of concepts, terminology and notation for geometric pattern matching, centred around the idea of a {\em transformation class}. After formally defining the concept of a transformation class, we provide detailed definitions of a number of specific transformation classes that are particularly relevant to pattern matching and pattern discovery in music, which is the primary application domain within which the framework has been developed. We then provide formal definitions of the notions of {\em match}, {\em occurrence}, {\em maximal match\/} and {\em maximal occurrence\/} and prove some results relating to these concepts. We then define and explore in detail the idea of an {\em occurrence set\/} and the more general notion of a {\em heterogeneous occurrence set}. Finally, we explore in detail the concept of {\em transformational equivalence}, including a consideration of {\em transformation groups}, along with the group-theoretic and transformational equivalence properties of selected transformation classes.

papers.title: NumPSLA -- An experimental research tool for pseudoline arrangements and order types
papers.abstract: We present a program for enumerating all pseudoline arrangements with a small number of pseudolines and abstract order types of small point sets. This program supports computer experiments with these structures, and it complements the order-type database of Aichholzer, Aurenhammer, and Krasser. This system makes it practical to explore the abstract order types for 12 points, and the pseudoline arrangements of 11 pseudolines.

papers.title: On the Column Number of Delta-Modular Matrices: an $O(m^2 \Delta)$ Bound via the Shifted Heller Constant
papers.abstract: In this paper, we build on the analysis initiated by Averkov and Schymura (2022) and prove that the shifted Heller constant for matrices with $m$ rows is at most $m^2 + m$ for all sufficiently large $m$. Consequently, the number of distinct columns of a $\Delta$-modular matrix $A \in Z^{m \times n}$ of rank $m$ is at most $O(m^2 \Delta)$. This improves upon the earlier bounds of $O(m^4 \Delta)$ and $O(m^2 \Delta^2)$.

papers.title: Capacitated Clustering with Few Extra Centers
papers.abstract: In capacitated $(k,z)$-clustering, we open $k$ centers and assign every client to a center within its capacity, minimizing the sum of $z$-th powers of the distances; $k$-median and $k$-means are the cases $z=1$ and $z=2$. We study polynomial-time algorithms that open $k+\lfloor\varepsilon k\rfloor$ centers but respect the capacities exactly. All ratios hold up to an additive $\delta$ for every fixed $\delta>0$. For uniform soft capacities in low dimensions, we obtain ratio $\beta-(\beta-1)\varepsilon$, where $\beta=3^z$ if the clients or the locations have bounded doubling dimension, and $\beta=\mathcal{B}_z<3^z$ for $z>1$ if the clients do and centers may lie anywhere in $\mathbb{R}^d$. This gives $3-2\varepsilon$ for $k$-median and $5-4\varepsilon$ for Euclidean $k$-means. We also obtain ratios bounded by a constant for hard capacities, and $1+(3^z-1)e^{-\varepsilon}$ for non-uniform soft capacities. These are the first polynomial-time ratios with $(1+\varepsilon)k$ centers that are bounded by a constant, apart from uniform $k$-median in the plane. For uniform $k$-median in general metrics, we obtain $3+2\ln(1/\varepsilon)$ with soft and $7+2\ln(1/\varepsilon)$ with hard capacities, improving the previous $O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\varepsilon))$. Splitting the clusters of a near-optimal uncapacitated solution into groups of at most $U$ clients, where $U$ is the capacity, gives fewer than $2k$ groups. With fewer centers, groups must share centers. Each extra center gives private centers to about two groups, since a center of an optimal solution that serves only such groups can be closed. Thus $\lfloor\varepsilon k\rfloor$ extra centers remove almost an $\varepsilon$-fraction of the extra cost caused by sharing.
